meta.description: Daily tracking state for F-1/SEVP/DS-2019 policy monitoring, focused on relevance to a Virginia Tech student who may need an extra semester to finish their degree.

items.title: DHS Final Rule: Fixed Time Period of Admission & Extension of Stay (ends Duration of Status) for F, J, I nonimmigrants
items.summary: DHS published a final rule (doc. 2026-14439) on Jul 17, 2026, ending open-ended Duration of Status for F-1 students, effective Sep 15, 2026. Students get a fixed 'Admit Until Date' capped at 4 years (24 months for language programs); anyone needing more time must file Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) with USCIS in addition to the existing DSO SEVIS extension -- the I-539 EOS filing fee is reported as $420 filed online / $470 by paper. A timely-filed EOS gives up to 240 days of authorized stay while pending. The rule also shortens the F-1 post-completion grace period from 60 to 30 days for anyone who travels/re-enters or gets an EOS approval after the effective date. Students already in D/S status who remain continuously in the U.S. without leaving/re-entering keep transition protections, but only up to a hard outside cap of Nov 14, 2030 (4 years + 60-day grace period measured from the Sep 15, 2026 effective date).
items.notes: No lawsuit had been filed and no Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution had passed as of this run (checked 2026-08-15, second check today). NAFSA remains publicly opposed. SEVP stakeholder webinar on the rule remains reported for Mon, Aug 31, 2026, 2-3pm ET. A WebSearch result surfaced a 'Campaign Legal Center: Order Granting Preliminary Injunction' and an Aug 3, 2026 injunction reference that looked promising, but targeted follow-up queries (lawsuit filings, NAFSA legal tracker, law-firm alerts through mid-August) found no actual injunction or filed lawsuit specific to this D/S rule -- that document appears to be an unrelated case surfaced by keyword overlap. Treating the rule's Sep 15, 2026 effective date as still on track pending confirmation either way. Separately, 30 U.S. Senators (led by Sen. Alex Padilla) sent an Aug 11, 2026 letter to Secretary of State Rubio pressing for faster F/M/J visa interview processing before fall term -- tracked as its own item below since it concerns visa *issuance* delays, not the D/S admission-period change itself, but is relevant context for any student who needs to travel and re-enter under the new rule. WebFetch remains unavailable (environment-level egress block); WebSearch is the sole research channel.

items.title: USCIS Policy Alert PA-2026-05: officers may deny incomplete filings without issuing an RFE/NOID first
items.summary: Effective Aug 5, 2026, USCIS updated Policy Manual guidance so adjudicators may, at their discretion, deny a benefit request lacking required initial evidence or failing to establish eligibility without first issuing an RFE or NOID, and may set RFE response deadlines shorter than the prior 12-week norm (the 14-day international-mail grace period was also eliminated). Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) or I-765 under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure.
items.notes: UPGRADED to Confirmed today: found the official USCIS newsroom alert (uscis.gov/newsroom/alerts/uscis-to-reduce-frivolous-immigration-benefits-requests-by-reinforcing-evidence-standards) and the underlying Policy Alert PA-2026-05 PDF (uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/policy-manual-updates/20260805-EvidentiaryStandards.pdf), which updates USCIS-PM E.6, E.9, and E.10, effective for requests pending or filed on/after Aug 5, 2026. Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 Extension of Stay under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure via RFE/NOID.

items.title: SEVP Broadcast Message BCM 2608-01: DSOs warned on CPT authorization liability, increased scrutiny
items.summary: On Aug 12, 2026, SEVP issued Broadcast Message 2608-01, 'Reminder of Liability for DSOs Regarding CPT Authorization,' to every PDSO/DSO at SEVP-certified schools. SEVP says it has observed a rise in Curricular Practical Training (CPT) authorizations that do not meet regulatory requirements -- specifically CPT not constituting an integral part of an established curriculum -- and is increasing scrutiny of CPT approvals. The message does not change the CPT regulation itself and DHS's July D/S final rule separately stated it 'does not prohibit or eliminate Day-1 CPT' and 'does not make substantive changes to CPT.' But it signals stepped-up enforcement: schools found authorizing CPT improperly risk investigation and loss of SEVP certification, and secondary reporting (Murthy Law, American Bazaar) frames this as SEVP tightening the screws on a work-authorization pathway many students -- including those weighing an extra semester -- rely on for practical training before or alongside OPT.
items.notes: New item found today via WebSearch (not in previous snapshot). Official ICE PDF (bcm260801.pdf) confirms the message and its Aug 12, 2026 date. No regulatory text has changed -- this is a compliance/enforcement reminder, not a rulemaking -- but relevant to track because it raises the stakes for any student using CPT as part of an extended-timeline plan. WebFetch could not render the PDF directly (egress-blocked); relying on WebSearch's rendering of the document plus consistent secondary-source description of its contents.

items.title: 30 Senators press State Dept (Rubio) to clear F/M/J student visa interview backlog before fall term
items.source: Office of Sen. Alex Padilla (official press release) / press reporting
items.summary: On Aug 11, 2026, 30 U.S. Senators led by Sen. Alex Padilla sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying 'no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates' during peak season, and asking the State Department to restore priority to F, M, and J visa interviews, extend interview waivers for vetted returning students, and boost consular staffing before fall term starts. The letter gives State 30 days to respond to 10 questions -- a deadline around Sep 10, 2026, after most fall terms have already begun. Not a rule change, but directly relevant to any F-1 student (including someone on an extended timeline) who needs to obtain a new visa stamp or renew one to travel and re-enter, especially once the Sep 15, 2026 D/S-to-fixed-admission-period transition takes effect.
items.notes: New item found today via WebSearch. Confirmed via the official Senate.gov press release from Sen. Padilla's office confirming the letter was sent; that the letter exists is confirmed, but the State Department has not yet responded (response due ~Sep 10, 2026) -- will track for a State Department reply or any change in interview-scheduling practice.

items.title: DHS regulatory review of OPT / STEM OPT (RIN 1653-AA97) — no NPRM published yet
items.summary: DHS confirmed in a Jan 9, 2026 letter it is re-evaluating the scope and duration of OPT and STEM OPT, with a rulemaking entry (RIN 1653-AA97, titled 'Practical Training') in the Spring 2026 Unified Regulatory Agenda covering worker protection, fraud prevention, national security, and SEVP oversight goals. As of this run, no Notice of Proposed Rulemaking has been published in the Federal Register. A single secondary source (americanbazaaronline.com, Aug 11, 2026) reports the government's own unified agenda lists an NPRM target of February 2027 for this rule. OPT and STEM OPT remain fully operational and unchanged today. Relevant because many students planning an extra semester are also relying on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT timing.
items.notes: No OPT/STEM OPT NPRM has been published as of 2026-08-15 (second check today). No new developments found. WebFetch remains egress-blocked; will keep watching for actual NPRM publication.

items.title: Reported $100,000 fee under consideration for OPT / post-completion work authorization
items.source: Press reporting (Forbes, Bloomberg, ICEF Monitor, The PIE News, Higher Ed Dive)
items.summary: Multiple outlets report the administration is weighing a $100,000 fee applicable to OPT employment authorization (and by extension STEM OPT), modeled on the now-struck-down $100,000 H-1B fee proclamation. As of this run, no signed proclamation or DHS proposed rule/fee schedule has been reported for an OPT fee -- unlike the H-1B fee, which was signed via proclamation on Sep 19, 2025 and then struck down by a federal judge on Jun 8, 2026. Immigration attorneys quoted say an OPT fee is unlikely to survive legal challenge absent Congressional authorization, citing that H-1B precedent plus a Jul 24, 2026 appellate rejection of the administration's appeal. Who would pay (student/university/employer) remains unresolved. Directly relevant to students weighing an extra semester who are also counting on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT to work in the U.S. afterward.
items.notes: Still no DHS/USCIS/.gov statement, proposed rule, or signed proclamation found confirming or denying this as of 2026-08-15 (second check today). No proclamation has been signed. Reporting continues to cite the First Circuit's rejection of the administration's appeal in the related H-1B $100,000 fee litigation as the key legal headwind to an OPT-fee proclamation surviving challenge.

items.title: NAFSA/JB International report: fall 2026 international enrollment projected to fall ~9.5% (~111,000 students) amid visa crackdown
items.source: NAFSA: Association of International Educators / JB International (research report, press reporting)
items.summary: A report released Aug 11, 2026 by NAFSA and research firm JB International, based on institutional responses to IIE's Spring 2026 Snapshot survey, projects fall 2026 international enrollment at U.S. colleges will fall about 9.5% (~111,000 fewer students), citing declining applications, visa-appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy (including the D/S final rule) as converging headwinds. Estimated economic impact: ~$3.4 billion in lost local spending and ~39,000-40,000 jobs. Supporting data point noted today: Common App reports international submissions down ~9% for the 2026-27 cycle (India -14%, Ghana -34%, Nigeria -17%), with consulates in India, China, and across Europe reporting limited/delayed appointment availability. This is a research/economic-impact projection rather than a new rule -- it is being tracked here as evidence of how seriously the sector expects the policy changes above to bite, which is relevant context (not itself an actionable status change) for a student weighing an extra semester.
items.notes: This is a private-association economic/enrollment projection, not a government policy claim, so there is no .gov document that would ever 'confirm' it in the same sense as the other items -- it is tracked as 'Reported, unconfirmed' per the tracker's default schema, but readers should treat that label as 'not a government-verifiable fact' rather than 'possibly false.' Additional corroborating detail found today via WebSearch (not a status change): IIE's Spring 2026 Snapshot survey reportedly found Jan-Mar 2026 new international enrollment down ~20% for bachelor's and ~24% for master's programs year-over-year, with 63% of institutions expecting further declines for 2026-27 vs. 11% expecting increases; ~85% of institutions cited 'restrictive government policies or issues obtaining a visa' as the primary driver. Could not reach nafsa.org directly this run (WebFetch fully egress-blocked today) to render the underlying report/PDF itself. Additional secondary corroboration found today: U.S. News (Aug 5, 2026) reports international enrollment slipping amid visa-rule anxiety, consistent with the NAFSA/JB International projection. Still a research/economic-impact projection, not a government document -- no .gov source will ever 'confirm' it in the same sense as the other items.
